messages:
elaine: Customer reported sustained 429s for Dedicated tenant `acme-corp` starting ~2026-03-05T17:30Z. They say nothing changed on their side. I traced a few request IDs and control-plane decisions show assignment to `cpu-pool-3` (small pool) instead of the expected `gold-dedicated` pool. Anyone seeing routing noise?

mike: Can you paste one example request id + control-plane decision log? Also, which config rollout went out last 24h?

elaine: request_id=rc-20260305-017, header: `X-Tier-Preference: [\"gold\"]`. Control plane trace: 
```
2026-03-05T17:31:02Z controlplane.decision request_id=rc-20260305-017 tenant=acme-corp matched_rule=route_by_tier assigned_pool=cpu-pool-3 reason="matched tier array index 0"
headers={"x-tier-preference":"[\"gold\"]","x-tenant":"acme-corp"}
```
Response downstream: 429 + `X-Assigned-Pool: cpu-pool-3`.

jess: Hmm. We rolled out controlplane:tier-array-eval v2 yesterday (deploy 6a9f2c). That change altered how tier arrays are parsed and the comparator we use. Ops noted minor perf win. @deploy-bot can you confirm?

deploy-bot: Deployment recorded: controlplane service v2026.03.04-6a9f2c (tier-array-eval). No rollbacks recorded.

sam: If the header is being parsed as a single string like "[\"gold\"]" instead of an actual array, the matching logic might fallback to a default comparator and hit the first eligible (smaller) pool. Can you share the raw header bytes?

elaine: raw header (from tcpdump): `X-Tier-Preference: ["gold"]` (no encoding, looks like how caller sends it).

mike: Repro steps I ran locally:
```bash
curl -v -H "X-Tier-Preference: [\"gold\"]" -H "X-Tenant: acme-corp" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# -> response 200 when routed to gold-dedicated, 429 when routed to cpu-pool-3
```
I instrumented controlplane decision with extra debug: it logs parsed_tiers as "[\"gold\"]" (string) for that request, not ["gold"] (array).

jess: That matches suspicion. The v2 parser change uses JSON.parse only when header is detected as JSON array via heuristics; there was a branch that returns the raw string on parse errors. It looks like an escaping/quote normalization regression means our heuristic treats the input as non-array and falls into legacy comparator that treats the value as a token which matches lower-priority rule.

sam: Why didn't autoscaler kick in on cpu-pool-3? I see the pool was allowed to scale but min_replicas is 1 and scale window is 3m; the spike lasted ~12m but rate limiter on that pool hit pool-level token bucket because many connections from this tenant were sticky. Also pool affinity was set to allow small-pool fallback for latency SLOs. So two failures: bad route selection + throttle enforcement on small pool.

mike: Immediate mitigation options: 1) hotfix parser to always treat bracketed header as JSON array; 2) add a routing override that maps tenant `acme-corp` -> gold-dedicated (tenant-affinity); 3) temporary rule to increase cpu-pool-3 capacity. I'm pushing a hotfix PR for parser now.

elaine: Can we also force-failover existing requests away from cpu-pool-3 for that tenant? Might be risky. I'd prefer tenant override while parser patch rolls out.

jess: Agreed. I'll apply a policy override (manual mapping) for `acme-corp` to `gold-dedicated` and monitor. Then we roll the parser hotfix to canary and verify. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/controlplane/pulls/8423 (parsing guard + unit tests).

deploy-bot: Hotpatch deployed to canary subsets at 2026-03-05T18:10Z (canary: 10% traffic).

mike: After override is live, I see 200 -> 99% for the sampled request ids. We'll keep canary patch for a bit and promote once we confirm array parsing tests pass.

sam: Follow-ups: add a regression test covering header forms: JSON-array (with/without spaces), comma-separated tokens, single-token string, and header casing variations. Also add an e2e that simulates a high-QPS tenant fallback to verify autoscaler + throttles interplay.

elaine: Noted. Customer notified: "we applied a routing override and pushed a fix to canary, monitoring for recovery". They acknowledged.

jess: Root cause summary for ticket: tier-array-eval v2 heuristic mis-classifies bracketed header as raw string in certain quoting/escape patterns, causing fallback comparator to match lower-priority pool -> traffic concentrated on small pool -> throttle. Fix: stricter JSON-array detection + unit tests; policy override for affected tenants applied; rollout to stable after canary.

mike: I'll close the high-priority incident once stable metrics hold for 30m. Current plan: monitor 1h, postmortem to cover rollout checks and add 3 tests.

sam: +1. Also log an action item to add a routing self-check that warns when a tenant suddenly shifts pool assignment distribution by >20% in 5m.

elaine: thanks all :thumbsup:
